## Overview

**Bardolemeu Romeo** is a human bard from one of the wealthiest and most influential families on the continent -- the Romeo family, owners of the largest and most prestigious theatres in the kingdom. Born into privilege, he rejected his inheritance after discovering the exploitation and censorship that sustained his family's empire. He now wanders the land, bringing music and art to those who cannot afford it, carrying only his mentor's old lute and the lessons that shaped him.

---

## Appearance

A well-dressed human with the easy charm of a born performer. His clothes are fine but practical -- travelling clothes that once belonged in a wardrobe of luxury. He carries an old lute -- his mentor's instrument, worn from years of use -- and moves with the confidence of someone who has always had a stage, even if the stage has now changed.

---

## Background

Bardolemeu was born into the Romeo family, one of the richest and most influential houses in Kythoria. His family owns the largest and most prestigious theatres in the kingdom -- venues where nobles, merchants, and powerful figures gather for grand spectacles. From an early age, he was taught that art existed to generate profit, win favours, and strengthen the family's influence. Every play was chosen to please the powerful, every musician hired was a tool to maintain prestige, and every round of applause was measured in coin.

But Bardolemeu could never see music that way.

While his parents treated artists as servants and discussed revenue, contracts, and political alliances, he found comfort with an old musician who worked in one of the family's theatres. Unlike everyone else, the old man never treated Bardolemeu as an heir. He taught him to play the lute, to sing, and above all, taught him that true art belongs to the people -- not to the rich or the powerful. He often said that a good song could survive for centuries, long after any empire or fortune had crumbled.

As Bardolemeu grew older, he discovered the darker truths behind his family's prestige. Artists were exploited -- paid little for their talent and discarded when they were no longer profitable. Shows were censored to please the nobles. Stories were altered to protect influential figures. Anyone who dared to challenge the family's interests found their career destroyed. To his parents, art had no inherent value. It was merely a product.

The old musician knew too many secrets. He knew how artists were silenced, how plays disappeared on the orders of powerful people, and how fear was used to control those who depended on the family's theatres to survive. One day, he vanished without a trace. Bardolemeu was told he had left in search of new stages, but he never believed that lie. He is certain the old man was silenced for knowing more than he should.

In that moment, Bardolemeu realised that if he stayed, he would become exactly like his parents.

That same night, he left the mansion without telling anyone. He took no jewellery, no gold, no part of the fortune that would one day be his. He took only his master's old lute and the lessons the man had left him. He made a promise to himself: he would never allow art to serve only those who already had everything.

The early days were hard. He went hungry, slept in the open, and discovered a world completely different from the one he was raised in. But it was also in this world that he found what his master had always tried to teach him. He saw a simple song unite strangers in a tavern, draw a smile from children who had never set foot in a theatre, and restore hope to people who had lost everything. He understood that music did not exist to feed the egos of the powerful or enrich those who exploited it -- it existed to inspire, to comfort, and to remind people that they are never truly alone.

Since then, he has wandered without a fixed destination. Every song he composes is a tribute to the man who showed him the true meaning of art. Every story he tells seeks to immortalise the deeds of those who will never set foot on the stage of the great theatres. And every performance he offers freely to those who have nothing is a way of proving that art is worth more when it is shared than when it is sold.

---

## Abilities

- **Bardic Magic**: Spells woven through music and performance
- **Bardic Inspiration**: Lifting spirits and empowering allies through art
- **Social Grace**: Raised in high society, comfortable in any gathering
- **Performance**: Singer, musician, storyteller, actor -- trained by his mentor

---

## Goals

1. Bring the joy of music and art to those who cannot afford it -- honouring his mentor's teachings
2. Prove that art's true value lies in the lives it touches, not the wealth it generates
3. Experience the world firsthand, beyond the filtered lens of wealth and privilege
4. Understand his connection to magic through art (his bardic awakening)
5. Potentially return to his family's theatres -- not to reclaim his inheritance, but to open the curtains to all who were excluded
